column1: # SURFACES WORTH WATCHING -- the list is DECLARED here, the verdict is DERIVED.
# docrender/tokenaudit.py reads this file, searches every stylesheet WE ship for
# each `probe`, and prints how many of our rules mention it. Zero means Material
# paints that surface and no theme token can change it.
# WHY A HAND-WRITTEN LIST AT ALL, given this repo has killed several. Because the
# alternative needs a manifest of every class MkDocs Material ships, which we do
# not have and would have to maintain -- a bigger hand-written list to avoid a
# smaller one. The split that makes this safe: a human says what is worth
# WATCHING, the build says what is TRUE.
# ⭐ AND THAT SPLIT JUST PAID OUT FOR THE FIRST TIME (2026-08-05). The admonition
# rows below flipped from ungoverned to governed WITH NO EDIT to this file, the
# day assets/admonition.css shipped, exactly as the design promised. The verdict
# was never stored here, so it could not go stale.
# ⚠️ THE NOTES CAN STILL GO STALE, AND TWO OF THEM DID. They said governing the
# callouts required a blocks table that does not exist -- and that was a real
# framing error, not just old prose: it conflated PAINTING the families Material
# ships (pure CSS, no vocabulary needed, done now) with INVENTING our own (which
# does need the table, and is still Q14). A row going stale costs a row nobody
# needed; a stale NOTE in the file whose whole job is honesty is worse.
# ⚑ Worth carrying to every row still listed here: "we do not own the vocabulary"
# is a reason we cannot ADD a family. It is not a reason we cannot PAINT the ones
# that exist. Check which of the two is actually missing before writing a row off.
# ADDING ONE is a row. `probe` is a plain substring matched against our selector
# text, so keep it specific enough not to collide: `.md-typeset` would match
# almost everything and prove nothing.
# surface   what a reader sees
# probe     substring searched in OUR selectors
# note      why it matters, and what it would take to govern it
surface
Admonition / callout blocks
column3: ✅ GOVERNED as of 2026-08-05, assets/admonition.css. Box, border, left edge, radius and shadow from the theme; the family colour from one of info / accent-2 / good / warn / bad / accent / ink-muted, mapped per Material type. Was the largest ungoverned surface on the site. Still NOT ours: the ICON GLYPH itself (Material ships the mask-image; we only tint it) and the ability to add a family Material does not have, which is Q14 and needs a blocks table.

column1: Admonition title bar
column3: ✅ GOVERNED 2026-08-05. A 12% wash of the family colour rather than a fill, so the title text can stay `ink` at any family colour -- a fill cannot promise that. Icon tinted via background-color on ::before.

column1: Collapsible blocks
column3: ✅ GOVERNED 2026-08-05. Every admonition rule carries a `details` selector beside it, so the `???` form is styled identically plus a hover wash on the summary. The disclosure arrow is tinted; its glyph is Material's.

column1: Tabbed content
column3: Tab labels, the active underline and the panel border. Material's, and the active colour follows its accent rather than ours. ⭐ NOW THE LARGEST UNGOVERNED SURFACE, and unlike the callouts it needs no vocabulary either -- the classes are Material's and stable. This is the next one to take.

column1: Search panel
column3: The overlay, the input, the result list and the term highlight.

column1: Footnotes
column3: The rule above them, the backref arrow and the numbering.

column1: Code block chrome
column3: Syntax colours come from a Pygments stylesheet, not from our tokens. Our --dr-code-bg only sets the surface behind it, so a theme change repaints the box and not the code. ⚠️ The one row here that genuinely needs more than CSS: Pygments emits its own class names and its own palette, so governing it means generating a Pygments sheet from the colour vector -- the data-1..4 tokens are the obvious candidates and have no consumer today.

column1: Blockquote
column3: The left rule and indent on a plain markdown quote. ⚠️ Note the overlap now: `!!! quote` IS governed and a `>` blockquote is not, so the same idea renders two ways depending on which syntax an author reached for.
